name: Grav-Board
description: A personal anti-gravity platform about the size of a surfboard. Hovers 1-3 meters off the ground and can reach moderate speeds. The technology is real but the power requirements are enormous — a grav-board burns through battery in 20 minutes of hard riding. Rich kids use them to commute across corporate campuses. In the lower tiers, a working grav-board is worth more than most people's apartments.
propulsion: Anti-gravity repulsion field, electric thrust vectoring
common_usage: Corporate campus commuting, recreation, status symbol. Competitive grav-board racing is a Tier 4-5 spectator sport.
story_hooks: A Tier 1 kid finds a damaged grav-board and repairs it — now every corp security team in the district wants to know where they got anti-grav tech
Grav-board racers are disappearing after entering a restricted airspace zone above the old industrial district
physical_description: A scarred polymer platform roughly 1.8 meters long and 0.6 meters wide, its surface pitted from impact with rain-slicked concrete and industrial debris. The underside bristles with exposed emitter arrays and heat-dissipation fins, their aluminum oxidized to dull gray. A central battery pack—bulky, always warm to the touch—dominates the topside, wrapped in fraying carbon-weave tape and crowned with flickering status LEDs that cycle through amber warnings. The deck itself is bare composite, grip-tape worn to slickness in high-contact zones.
visual_prompt: gritty neo-noir grav-board hovering above wet concrete, worn polymer deck with exposed aluminum emitters, weathered carbon-weave battery housing, flickering amber LED indicators, rain-slicked surface, industrial setting, detailed product photography, dark moody lighting, cyberpunk tech worn practical not flashy, high contrast shadows, realistic material deterioration
